profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record in Wrocław, one of Poland's largest cities and a major regional technology and business-outsourcing hub, tagged telecom=data_center, is named itQ Data Center. The name directly and explicitly references IT and data-center services ("itQ" evoking "IT quality" or a similar IT-branding construction, combined with "Data Center" spelled out plainly), making this one of the more plausible genuine data-center candidates among the lower-information European records reviewed this session, in contrast to names that give no computing signal or actively suggest an unrelated business. Wrocław has attracted substantial technology-sector investment, including business process outsourcing, software development, and some data-center and cloud infrastructure, as part of Poland's broader growth as a Central European technology hub. However, no operator website, press coverage, or Polish business registration (KRS) could be located and confirmed this session because search-tool quota was exhausted, so this entry cannot confirm itQ's specific capacity, service offering, or ownership, and is filed as a plausible genuine small data-center business pending further research.

reading.body:
itQ Data Center is an unverified OpenStreetMap record in Wrocław, Poland, with no capacity figure and no confirmed operator.

The record carries a name that plainly signals IT and data-center services, and it sits in one of Poland's largest cities and a growing technology and business-outsourcing hub. That combination makes it a plausible genuine small facility rather than a mislabeled building. The only source is an OpenStreetMap tagging review, and the research status is exhausted, meaning the operator website, press coverage, and Polish business registration were not confirmed.

For AI specifically, the entry contributes nothing measurable. It reports zero megawatts, which is a placeholder rather than a finding, and it names no operator, no capacity, and no service offering. A reader cannot tell from this data whether the site hosts compute, colocation racks, or merely network equipment.

What the data does establish is location: a facility in a Central European tech city, 6.8 miles from Copernicus Wrocław Airport. That is a siting fact, not a power or compute fact. The gap between a plausible name and a confirmed facility is the whole story here, and it is the gap that any count of European data centers has to close before it can be used to reason about AI capacity.
